beads.title: production.mjs: lift the fan-out restriction via explicit shares
beads.body:
FACTORIO.md's oracle-stack table and the vision both name this as the single most valuable thing left to build: production.mjs v1 refuses fan-out outright, and its own header explains why — 'with fan-out allowed, how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for'. This ticket does NOT ask the oracle to solve for that split (a real LP, out of scope). It asks the network literal to supply the split explicitly, which is enough to turn every future fan-out level from ungradeable into gradeable, exactly as gate 5 itself did for sources/sinks.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. Nothing else.

Design (continues 'Fan-out ticket scoped to explicit-share' and 'Share validation groups by RESOLVED resource, not by node' from memory — R5):

1. An edge MAY carry an optional numeric `share` field, `0 < share <= 1`.
2. In `analyse()`, after resolving each edge's shared resource exactly as today (unknown-node and shared-resource checks unchanged), group a node's OUTGOING edges by (from, resolvedResource) — not by `from` alone. A processor with two different outputs must be able to fan out each output independently without one group's validation touching the other.
3. Within a group of size 1 (today's only legal shape): if `share` is present it must be in (0, 1]; if absent, default to 1. This must reproduce every existing single-edge case byte-for-byte — the whole existing selftest's positive cases (the basic chain, both convergence cases, the capacity-cap case) must keep passing unmodified, since none of them set `share` and all expect share=1 behaviour.
4. Within a group of size > 1 (real fan-out): EVERY edge in that group MUST carry an explicit numeric `share` in (0, 1], or throw `production: node "${from}" splits resource "${resource}" without an explicit share (fan-out)`. Keep the substring 'fan-out' in that message so the EXISTING control in production.selftest.mjs — two edges from one source, neither carrying a share, asserted to throw with a message including 'fan-out' — keeps passing without modification.
5. Sum the group's shares. If the sum exceeds 1 (allow a small float epsilon, e.g. 1e-9), throw `production: node "${from}" over-allocates resource "${resource}" (shares sum to ${sum})`. Do NOT require the sum to equal exactly 1 — a network may deliberately leave part of an output unrouted (see the 'learned' decision above).
6. `outEdges` entries carry the resolved `share` (explicit or defaulted). In `feasible()`'s emission loop, multiply the delivered amount by that share: `dest[resource] += (out[resource] || 0) * share`. `inDegree`/topological-sort bookkeeping is unchanged — it already counts one increment per edge, regardless of share.
7. Update the file's header comment (lines ~9-25) to describe the new explicit-share behaviour in place of the flat 'v1 disallows FAN-OUT' sentence — state plainly that the SPLIT is supplied by the network, not solved for, and that this is a deliberate, narrower feature than a general LP.

New test coverage to add to production.selftest.mjs, in the house style already established (every positive case paired with a CONTROL, every number hand-computed — see the file's own header on why):
 - A source (rate 10, resource x) fanning to two sinks via edges with shares 0.3 and 0.7: hand-calc achieved = 3 and 7, margins computed and asserted against the sinks' demands.
 - CONTROL: same two edges with shares 0.3 and 0.8 (sum 1.1) — throws, message includes 'over-allocate'.
 - CONTROL: same two edges, one with an explicit share and the sibling missing `share` — throws, message includes 'fan-out' (a group is all-explicit or entirely rejected, never a mix with an implicit member).
 - CONTROL (regression, must not need editing): the file's existing two-sink-no-shares fan-out case still throws with 'fan-out' in the message, and its paired single-edge CONTROL still passes.
 - A processor with two distinct outputs (e.g. 'gear' and 'scrap'), where 'gear' fans to two sinks with shares summing to 1 and 'scrap' goes to a third sink via a single edge with no `share` field: assert the 'scrap' edge is unaffected by the 'gear' group's multi-edge validation — this is the resolved-resource, not-by-node grouping rule, and it is the one behaviour most likely to regress silently if implemented per-node instead.
 - A single edge with an explicit share < 1 (e.g. 0.6) and nothing else consuming the rest: assert the sink receives exactly rate*0.6, confirming partial-routing is legal and the unrouted remainder is simply not delivered anywhere (not an error).
 - Re-run (or re-assert unchanged) every existing positive fixture in the file — basic chain, both convergence cases, capacity-cap case, band() cases, determinism check — to confirm byte-identical behaviour with no `share` field present anywhere in them.

[turn 15 — done] Lifted production.mjs's flat fan-out ban and replaced it with explicit-share fan-out: an edge may carry an optional numeric `share` in (0, 1]. analyse() now resolves each edge's shared resource in a first pass (unchanged from before), then groups a node's outgoing edges by (from, RESOLVED resource) rather than by `from` alone, so a processor with two distinct outputs fans each out independently. A group of one edge defaults share to 1 when absent (reproducing every pre-existing single-edge case byte-for-byte, since none of them set `share`), and a group of more than one edge requires every member to carry an explicit share, throwing a message containing 'fan-out' otherwise, or 'over-allocate' if the group's shares sum above 1 (with a 1e-9 float epsilon). feasible()'s emission loop now multiplies delivered amount by the resolved share, so an unrouted remainder (shares summing to less than 1) is simply not delivered anywhere rather than being an error. Also rewrote the file's header comment to describe explicit-share fan-out instead of the old flat prohibition. Added the ticket's full new test coverage to production.selftest.mjs: a two-sink explicit-share split with hand-computed achieved/margin, a CONTROL for shares summing over 1, a CONTROL for one explicit + one implicit sibling in the same group, a CONTROL for a single partial share leaving the remainder unrouted, and a resolved-resource-not-by-node grouping case (a processor with 'gear' fanning to two sinks and 'scrap' going to a third sink unaffected by the gear group's validation). Also renamed the old no-share fan-out block's heading and kept its two existing assertions (including the CONTROL) unmodified, and left every pre-existing positive fixture (basic chain, both convergence cases, capacity-cap case, all band() cases, determinism check) completely untouched — none of them set `share`, so they exercise the new default-to-1 single-edge path and should behave identically to before. NOTE: I have Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, so `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs` (this ticket's own GATE) could not be executed in-turn. Every new assertion's expected number was hand-traced through analyse()/feasible() as edited (10*0.3=3, 10*0.7=7, margin=min(0.5,1/6)=1/6, 10*0.6=6 with margin (6-5)/5=0.2, gear group 10*0.4=4 and 10*0.6=6, scrap group defaulted-share 10*1=10) and every existing fixture was confirmed to carry no `share` field anywhere, so the single-edge default-to-1 path is a byte-for-byte no-op for them. This is the eleventh class-a/creates-gate-adjacent ticket in a row with this exact structural gap (see the standing finding below) — confidence is high from the hand-trace but it is inference, not execution.

beads.title: Fan-out groups by (from, resolved resource) using nested Maps, not a joined string key
beads.body: Considered keying the group-by step with a single string like `${from}\u0000${resource}` or `${from} ${resource}`, then rejected both: a NUL separator risks the exact NUL-byte-in-source class of bug the ledger already has a dead-end for (a scripted edit that put NUL bytes into a .mjs source and every test still passed), and a space separator could in principle collide if a node id or resource string itself contained the separator character (e.g. from="a b", resource="c" vs from="a", resource="b c"). Used `Map<from, Map<resource, edges[]>>` instead — no string concatenation, no collision risk, and iteration order is still insertion order (from-first, then resource-first-seen-within-that-from), which is deterministic and matches the edges array's original order closely enough that no existing ordering-dependent behavior (e.g. which error fires first) changed for any single-group-per-from case. This only matters when node ids or resource names contain unusual characters, which no current fixture does, but nested maps cost nothing extra and remove the risk entirely.

beads.title: Share validity for a lone (non-fan-out) edge is validated too, not just defaulted
beads.body: The ticket's point 3 says 'if share is present it must be in (0,1]; if absent, default to 1' for a group of size 1 — read literally as also applying if a caller supplies an out-of-range share (e.g. 1.5 or -1 or 0) on a single edge with no sibling. Added that check even though no ticket test case exercises it, because leaving a size-1 group's explicit share unvalidated would silently accept a share > 1 (over-delivering more than the source's actual rate would suggest) or <= 0 (delivering nothing or negative amounts) with no error at all — an inconsistency with the size>1 case, which does validate every member's share range. Reverses cleanly: delete the `else if` branch in the group.length===1 arm if this is judged out of scope.

beads.title: production.mjs: autoSplit() — closed-form optimal split for the simplest fan-out case (direct source→sinks, provably max-min fair)
beads.body:
Vision priority 1 calls fan-out 'the ceiling, and the real puzzle' and quotes production.mjs's own former header: 'how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for.' Turn 15 (lp-34239d, done) built the prerequisite the vision asked for first — the network literal can now SPECIFY a split via explicit per-edge `share`, and feasible() computes it correctly — but explicitly scoped OUT the actual solving: 'An optimizer that searches over shares is a distinct, later ticket once this lands' (lp-dc4659, in memory). This ticket is that later ticket, scoped to the one sub-case that has a closed-form, provably-optimal answer — not the general multi-hop LP, which stays out of scope for one turn exactly as it did at turn 15.

The sub-case: a node's fan-out group (edges sharing one (from, RESOLVED resource) group, same grouping analyse() already uses) where (a) no edge in the group carries an explicit `share`, (b) every edge's `to` node is kind 'sink', and (c) each such sink has exactly one incoming edge in the WHOLE network (this fan-out edge is its only supply — so its `demand` is exactly what a fair share should cover, not confounded by supply from elsewhere). For that sub-case there is a closed-form optimal split: allocate proportional to demand, `share_i = demand_i / sum(demand_j over the group)`. This is the unique split maximizing the group's minimum margin: margin_i = (S*share_i - demand_i)/demand_i = S*(share_i/demand_i) - 1, so maximizing min_i margin_i means maximizing min_i(share_i/demand_i) subject to sum(share_i) <= 1 — maximized exactly when every share_i/demand_i is equal (moving budget from a higher ratio to a lower one always raises the min until they're equal), which is exactly proportional allocation. Any group NOT matching (a)/(b)/(c) — an explicit share already present, a destination that's a processor, or a sink fed from more than one edge — is left completely untouched; feeding it to feasible() unchanged still throws exactly as today. This keeps the change strictly additive: nothing that works today changes behavior.

Add to plant/production.mjs: `export function autoSplit(network)` — pure, returns a new `{ nodes, edges }` (nodes may be the same reference; edges is a new array; never mutates the input). For each qualifying group, replace its edges with copies carrying the computed `share`; every other edge (including edges in non-qualifying groups) is copied through unchanged. Callers pass the result to feasible()/analyse() exactly as any other network literal — autoSplit does not call feasible() itself and has no knowledge of margins beyond the ratio identity above. Update the file's header comment to note this new function exists and precisely what it does NOT do (solve the general multi-hop case).

Gate (already exists, extend it): node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. New section 'autoSplit() — closed-form split for the simplest fan-out case':
 - Source rate 100, resource x, two direct sinks demand 30 and 70 (each sink's only inbound edge, no explicit shares). autoSplit fills share1=0.3, share2=0.7 (hand calc: 30/100, 70/100). feasible() on the result: achieved.s1=30, achieved.s2=70 exactly; margin_s1=(30-30)/30=0, margin_s2=(70-70)/70=0 — assert BOTH margins equal 0, the hand-provable signature of the max-min-optimal split (equalized ratios), not just 'feasible'.
 - Same shape, source rate dropped to 60 (infeasible even optimally split): shares stay 0.3/0.7 (proportional to demand, unchanged by feasibility) -> achieved.s1=18, achieved.s2=42 -> margin_s1=(18-30)/30=-0.4, margin_s2=(42-70)/70=-0.4 — assert both margins equal -0.4 exactly, proving the fairness property holds even when short (neither sink is starved to protect the other).
 - CONTROL: same two-sink shape but one edge already carries an explicit share (e.g. 0.5) — assert autoSplit(network) leaves the edges array byte-identical to the input (JSON.stringify equal): a partially-explicit group is never touched, matching analyse()'s existing all-or-none rule.
 - CONTROL: a fan-out group whose second edge targets a processor, not a sink — assert autoSplit leaves it untouched (byte-identical edges) and that calling feasible() on the untouched result still throws with 'fan-out' in the message, exactly as before this ticket.
 - CONTROL: a sink with two incoming edges overall (this fan-out edge plus one more from a different source) — assert autoSplit leaves that group untouched too.
 - CONTROL: a single-edge (non-fan-out) group — assert autoSplit is a complete no-op (byte-identical network), and pass one of the file's existing single-edge fixtures through autoSplit before feasible() to confirm identical achieved/margin to calling feasible() directly.
 - No-mutation check: JSON.stringify of the input network is unchanged after calling autoSplit (same pattern level-view.selftest.mjs already uses for withSourceRate).

Bounded paths (R3): plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. Independent (R4): does not touch level-view.js, any levels/*.mjs file, or index.html — no ordering dependency on the drawLevel proposal below; either can land first or alone. Reversible (R6): autoSplit is a new export nothing existing calls, so a bad attempt reverts cleanly with zero effect on feasible()/analyse()'s existing behavior.

[turn 16 — done] Added autoSplit(network) to plant/production.mjs: a pure function that fills in the missing `share` field for the one fan-out sub-case that has a closed-form, provably-optimal answer — a direct source-or-processor -> sink fan-out, grouped by (from, RESOLVED resource) exactly as analyse() groups them, where every edge in the group carries no explicit share yet, every destination is kind 'sink', and each such sink has exactly one incoming edge in the whole network. Qualifying groups get share_i = demand_i / sum(demand_j), the proportional-to-demand split that is the unique max-min-fair allocation (worked in the ticket and restated in the function's docstring). Every edge outside a qualifying group — explicit share already present, destination not a sink, or a sink fed from elsewhere too — is copied through byte-identical; feasible() on an untouched network behaves exactly as before this ticket, including still throwing on an un-split fan-out. autoSplit never mutates its input (new edges array of new edge objects; nodes reference passed through unchanged) and never calls feasible() itself. Extended plant/test/production.selftest.mjs with a new section covering: the closed-form split and its zero-margin signature on both sides of the fan-out; the same shares surviving an infeasible (starved) source with both sinks margin -0.4 (proving neither is starved to protect the other); and four untouched-CONTROL cases (explicit share already on a sibling edge, a non-sink destination with the feasible() throw re-verified, a sink with a second supplier elsewhere in the network, and a single-edge non-fan-out group including a before/after equivalence check against calling feasible() directly) plus a no-mutation check. Every new number was hand-derived from the demand values in the fixtures (30/100=0.3, 70/100=0.7, 60*0.3=18, 60*0.7=42, resulting margins (18-30)/30=-0.4 and (42-70)/70=-0.4) and checked with the same 1e-12 tolerance pattern the rest of the file already uses.

beads.title: level-view.js: drawLevel must render every outgoing edge, not just the last one per node
beads.body:
level-view.js's drawLevel() builds `next = new Map(level.edges.map((e) => [e.from, e.to]))` (level-view.js:49) — a Map keyed by a node's id, so a SECOND outgoing edge from the same node silently overwrites the first and only one arrow is ever drawn. The comment directly above it (level-view.js:42-44) says why this was believed safe: 'Only the INCOMING side ever fans in — production.mjs v1 caps every node at one outgoing edge.' That comment is now wrong: turn 15 (lp-34239d, done) lifted that cap — production.mjs's analyse()/feasible() fully supports a node fanning one resource out across multiple edges via explicit `share` fields (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' section). So today the oracle can express a network the renderer silently corrupts: any level with a real fan-out edge would report correct feasible()/margin numbers while drawLevel() draws only the LAST of that node's edges and drops every other one — a visitor would see one arrow and a verdict that doesn't match what is on screen. This was flagged and deliberately deferred at the time (lp-fdd8a1: 'did not pair the fan-out oracle ticket with a level-view.js rendering fix... left for a follow-up turn once the oracle change lands and an actual level needs it') — the oracle change has now landed, so this is that follow-up.

Fix, bounded to plant/level-view.js only:
1. Change `next` to a Map<fromId, Array<{to, share}>> — collect every outgoing edge per node, in `level.edges` order, instead of overwriting.
2. In the arrow-drawing loop, iterate every entry in each node's array and draw one arrow per edge (today's single connecting-line-plus-arrowhead `<path>` pair, unchanged, just repeated per edge instead of per node). Multiple arrows leaving the same box and multiple arrows landing on the same box are both legal and must all render — do not dedupe by destination.
3. Update the stale comment at level-view.js:42-44 to describe the current, correct scope: a node MAY have more than one outgoing edge (fan-out, explicit share), and every one of them renders.

No change to production.mjs, to any levels/*.mjs file, or to drawLevel's column-layout logic (columns are keyed off `incoming`, which is already correct and untouched) — this is exactly and only the outgoing-arrow bug.

Gate (already exists, extend it): node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs. Add a new 'drawLevel: fan-out — a node with two outgoing edges must render both arrows, not just the last' case reusing production.selftest.mjs's own hand-verified explicit-share fixture (source rate 10, resource x, edges src->s1 share 0.3 and src->s2 share 0.7 — margins already hand-computed there as 0.5 and 1/6): call drawLevel on it and assert (a) it does not throw, (b) all three node ids ('src','s1','s2') each appear exactly once as boxes, (c) the rendered output contains exactly 4 `<path` elements (2 per edge: the connecting line plus its arrowhead, matching the existing single-chain test's convention of exactly 2 `<path` elements for exactly 1 edge) — under today's buggy Map this fixture renders only 2 `<path` elements (the second edge is silently dropped), so this assertion is a real regression check, not a tautology. Also re-run (unmodified) the file's existing single-chain and convergence cases to confirm neither regresses — both have every node's out-degree <= 1 already, so the fix is a no-op for them by construction.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/level-view.js, plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs. Independent (R4): touches neither production.mjs nor any levels/*.mjs file, so it has no ordering dependency on the autoSplit proposal above. Reversible (R6): a bad attempt reverts two files; nothing else in the tree calls drawLevel with a multi-edge network today, so there is no other caller to break.

[turn 23 — done] Fixed drawLevel() in plant/level-view.js to render every outgoing edge from a node instead of only the last one. The `next` lookup was a Map<fromId, toId> built from level.edges, so a second outgoing edge from the same node silently overwrote the first entry in the Map constructor. Changed it to a Map<fromId, Array<toId>> seeded from level.nodes (so every node has an entry, even one with zero outgoing edges) and populated by pushing every edge's `to` onto its `from` node's array, in level.edges order. The arrow-drawing loop now iterates every toId per fromId and draws the existing per-edge <path> pair (connecting line + arrowhead) once per edge, so N outgoing edges from one node now produce N arrows instead of 1. Also rewrote the stale comment at level-view.js:42-46, which claimed production.mjs still caps every node at one outgoing edge -- that cap was lifted by turn 15's fan-out work (lp-34239d), which is the whole reason this bug is now reachable. Column layout, box positions and box rendering are untouched -- only the outgoing-edge collection and the arrow-drawing loop changed. Added a new 'drawLevel: fan-out' test case to plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs reusing production.selftest.mjs's own hand-verified explicit-share fixture (source rate 10, resource x, src->s1 share 0.3, src->s2 share 0.7), asserting drawLevel does not throw, each of the three node ids appears exactly once as a box, and the output contains exactly 4 <path elements (2 per edge x 2 edges) -- under the old Map this fixture would render only 2 <path elements since the second edge overwrote the first. Did not modify or re-run the existing single-chain and convergence test cases in that file; both have every node's out-degree <= 1 by construction so the fix is a structural no-op for them, but I could not execute node to confirm this turn's tool grant is Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash.

beads.title: autoSplit() qualification is judged edge-by-edge inside a group, not group-by-group
beads.body: A group qualifies only if EVERY edge in it independently satisfies (a) no pre-existing share, (b) sink destination, (c) sole supplier of that sink. One disqualifying edge (e.g. one sibling already carrying an explicit share, or one destination being a processor) disqualifies the WHOLE group, not just that edge — matching analyse()'s existing all-or-none rule for explicit shares ("a group is all-explicit or entirely rejected, never a mix", already asserted in the pre-existing CONTROL block). This keeps autoSplit's output always feeding a network that is either fully resolved for that group or fully untouched, never a partial fill that could silently violate analyse()'s own invariant. Reversing this (per-edge partial fill) would need re-deriving what analyse() does with a group half-explicit-half-inferred, which is exactly the ambiguity the existing all-or-none rule was written to avoid.

beads.title: autoSplit's proportional fan-out does not produce 'one sink starved to feed the other' — it produces equal-percentage, unequal-absolute shortfall
beads.body: The ticket's framing ('losing looks like one sink starved to feed the other') suggested a favor-one-over-the-other dynamic. autoSplit()'s actual formula (share_i = demand_i / totalDemand, proved max-min-optimal in production.mjs's own header, and already exercised by production.selftest.mjs's autoSplit block) gives every sink the SAME percentage shortfall when supply is short — nobody is favored, and this turn's CONTROL A explicitly asserts marginA === marginB at rate 60. What DOES differ between the two sinks is the ABSOLUTE unit count: stockpileB (demand 70) loses 28 units to stockpileA's 12 at the same rate cut, simply because it demands more. I built the level and its test around this corrected, actually-true property rather than the ticket's literal wording. Reversal condition: if a future ticket wants a real favor-one-sink lever, it needs explicit per-edge share (already supported, see production.selftest's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' block) on a level whose network is NOT run through autoSplit — that is a different, not-yet-built level.

beads.title: LEVEL_5: the first level where the player's own explicit-share choice decides who gets fed, not a formula
beads.body:
LEVEL_4 (turn 18-19, done) uses autoSplit() to divide a source's output automatically -- proportional to demand, no player choice in HOW it splits, only in the shared rate. Vision priority 1 calls the actual decision 'splitting a shared output between competing consumers... the genre's central decision', and that decision is exactly what autoSplit removes from the player's hands. production.mjs already supports the other half of fan-out -- an explicit per-edge `share` the network literal sets directly (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' section, landed turn 15/lp-34239d) -- and no level exercises it as a player lever. This ticket is that level: the first one where the player's OWN choice, not a formula, decides which of two competing sinks gets fed.

Shape: one source `well` (resource water, rate 100) fanning out over two EXPLICIT-share edges to two sinks, `fieldA` (demand 30) and `fieldB` (demand 50):

  well --share shareA--> fieldA
  well --share (1-shareA)--> fieldB

Because the two shares are defined as `shareA` and `1 - shareA`, they always sum to exactly 1 -- the network is always LEGAL (production.mjs's 'over-allocate' refusal is only reachable above sum 1; the (0,1] per-edge bound is only violated at the extremes shareA=0 or shareA=1, both outside this level's intended play range) -- so this level is entirely about the FEASIBILITY trade-off (who gets shorted), not the illegal-network throw, which stays untouched and out of scope.

achievedA = 100*shareA, achievedB = 100*(1-shareA). Both sinks are simultaneously fed (ok=true, no deficits) exactly when shareA is in [0.30, 0.50] -- a real window, not a knife-edge: shareA >= 30/100 = 0.30 (else fieldA short) and shareA <= 0.50 (else fieldB short, since 1-shareA must be >= 50/100 = 0.50). The optimal point (equal margins on both sinks, matching autoSplit's own proportional-fairness proof already in production.mjs's docstring) is shareA = 30/80 = 0.375, giving margin 0.25 on both sinks (band 'comfortable').

Ship LEVEL_5 with shareA = 0.30 -- the LOW edge of the valid window: fieldA is exactly met (margin 0) and fieldB has slack (margin 0.4), overall margin 0, band 'tight' -- the same 'opens feasible, barely' texture LEVEL_1/LEVEL_3/LEVEL_4 all ship with. A future slider nudged up toward fieldB improves both sinks up to 0.375, then trades fieldA's margin away again past it; push far enough past 0.50 and fieldA keeps gaining while fieldB starves, and dropping below 0.30 starves fieldA while fieldB gains -- two distinct, opposite failure directions from one lever, which no existing level has (LEVEL_1/2/3 each have exactly one failure direction; LEVEL_4's failure is symmetric, not directional).

Write plant/levels/level5.mjs exporting:
  - `LEVEL_5` -- the network above, shares literal (0.3, 0.7), matching the shape and header-comment style of levels/level1.mjs through level4.mjs (explain the shape and the hand-computed shipped numbers).
  - `withShareA(level, shareA)` -- a level-local helper (do NOT add this to level-view.js -- lp-bc6980 is an open, ready ticket editing that exact file's edge-handling logic right now, and touching it here risks a collision; level2.mjs's SMELTER_OPTIONS is the precedent for a level keeping level-specific helpers in its own module rather than the shared one). Returns a new level object with the edge whose `to` is `fieldA` given `share: shareA` and the edge whose `to` is `fieldB` given `share: 1 - shareA` (matched by the edge's `to` field, not array position), every other field and node byte-identical, input never mutated -- same contract as `withSourceRate`/`withProcessorCapacity` in level-view.js.

Gate (does not exist yet -- creates it): node plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs, mirroring level4.selftest.mjs's house style (every number hand-computed, every positive case paired with a CONTROL, a no-mutation check). Required cases:
  1. Shipped LEVEL_5 (shareA=0.3): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===30, achieved.fieldB===70, margin===0 (hand calc: min((30-30)/30, (70-50)/50) = min(0, 0.4) = 0), band(margin)==='tight'.
  2. withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.5) (the other window edge): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===50, achieved.fieldB===50, margin===0, band==='tight'.
  3. withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.375) (the fair-split optimum): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===37.5, achieved.fieldB===62.5, marginA===marginB===0.25 (assert equality, the max-min-fair signature), overall margin===0.25, band==='comfortable'.
  4. CONTROL -- withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.2) (favoring fieldB too far): ok===false, exactly one deficit naming 'fieldA', achieved.fieldA===20, margin===(20-30)/30===-1/3, band==='infeasible'; assert fieldB is NOT short (achieved.fieldB===80 >= demand 50).
  5. CONTROL -- withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.6) (favoring fieldA too far): ok===false, exactly one deficit naming 'fieldB', achieved.fieldB===40, margin===(40-50)/50===-0.2, band==='infeasible'; assert fieldA is NOT short (achieved.fieldA===60 >= demand 30).
  6. No-throw invariant: for shareA in {0.05, 0.3, 0.375, 0.5, 0.95}, feasible(withShareA(LEVEL_5, shareA)) does not throw (shares always sum to exactly 1, always legal) -- a direct check that this level, unlike LEVEL_4's autoSplit path, never needs a try/catch.
  7. No-mutation: withShareA(LEVEL_5, x) leaves LEVEL_5 itself byte-identical (JSON.stringify unchanged), matching every other level's own no-mutation case.

  1. A single source, no other nodes, no edges: `{ nodes: [{ kind: 'source', id: 'src', resource: 'iron', rate: 10 }], edges: [] }`. Assert `feasible()` does not throw (one node, empty edges, topological sort trivially succeeds). Assert `result.ok === true`, `result.margin === 0` (not `Infinity`, not `NaN` -- the exact fallback value), `result.deficits.length === 0`, and `JSON.stringify(result.achieved) === '{}'` (achieved is only ever populated by walking sink nodes in the topological loop, and there are none).
  2.   3. Cross-check against the already-tested `band()`: assert `band(result.margin) === 'tight'` for case 1 -- margin 0 falls in band()'s already-pinned `[0, tight)` bracket (the file's existing band() section already asserts the 0.02 level-1 margin is 'tight'), so this is a real cross-check against already-passing code, not a new assumption about where 0 belongs.

beads.body:

beads.title: verdictLine() must report every sink that fell short, not just v.deficits[0]
beads.body:
BUG, CONFIRMED REACHABLE IN PLAY. plant/level-view.js's verdictLine() fail-path is:

  const d = v.deficits[0];
  return d ? `✗ ${d.sinkId} wanted ${d.demand} ${d.resource} and got ${d.achieved}. Short by ...` : '✗ infeasible';

This only ever describes the FIRST entry in v.deficits. plant/production.mjs's feasible() can return more than one deficit — plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's convergence and fan-out blocks exercise this, and plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs's own 'CONTROL A — rate dropped to 60' fixture asserts `r.deficits.length === 2` (both stockpileA and stockpileB short, by different absolute amounts — see that file's comment 'the new lesson'). Rate 60 is not a synthetic edge case: it is exactly the minimum of the ore4 `<input type="range" min="60" ...>` slider wired into plant/index.html for LEVEL_4, so a visitor who drags that slider all the way down reaches this state during ordinary play. drawLevel() already handles multiple deficits correctly — `verdict.deficits.some((d) => d.sinkId === n.id)` reddens EVERY starved sink's box, not just one — so the diagram and the verdict text visibly disagree: two red boxes, one sentence.

This is squarely the vision's playability bar: 'an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for' has to be a legible refusal, and right now the refusal a player provoked on LEVEL_4's worst case is reported as half of what actually happened.

SCOPE. Change verdictLine()'s fail branch to describe every entry in v.deficits (LEVEL_1/2/3's single-sink shape is unaffected — for them v.deficits.length is always 0 or 1, so existing behavior and existing test assertions must not change). Do not touch the ok-path's margin-naming (which sink sets the reported margin) — that's a softer, separate question and out of scope here; do not touch drawLevel() or its edge-drawing logic at all (lp-bc6980 is open against that same function right now — this ticket must not collide with it).

GATE (R2): node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs — already exists and already covers verdictLine's ok-path and single-deficit fail-path (see its header on the 'confident lie' risk: index.html renders verdictLine's return value directly, so a drift here is a wrong verdict presented as a right one). Add a new case reusing an inline two-sink, both-short fixture in the same style as its existing 'drawLevel: convergence' block (construct the network locally rather than importing plant/levels/level4.mjs, per that file's own stated independence rule so this ticket carries no ordering dependency on LEVEL_4's module — R4) — assert the returned string names BOTH starved sinks' ids, not just one. Keep the existing single-deficit assertions (level1.selftest.mjs's starved fixture) passing unchanged, and add a control confirming the old truncate-to-one-message shape does not silently still satisfy the new assertions (e.g. assert the string's occurrence count of each sink id, not just `.includes`).

REVERSIBLE (R6): pure string-formatting change to one function; a failed attempt is a revert with no other state to unwind.

MEMORY THIS CARRIES (R5): the level-view.selftest.mjs header's own 'confident lie' framing; lp-a427fe's 6/6-mutation-killed trust in production.mjs's deficits as ground truth; the LEVEL_4 module comment naming 'both sinks fall short... by different amounts' as its entire pedagogical point, which the current verdict text fails to actually say.

The v.deficits.length === 0 fallback to '✗ infeasible' is preserved unchanged, and the single-deficit case reduces to the same wording as before (one clause, no join separator visible) so the existing 'fail path: unchanged by this edit' test still passes untouched. Added one new test block to plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs with an inline two-sink fan-out fixture (source rate 10, explicit shares 0.3/0.7 to two sinks demanding 5 and 8) that reproduces the same 'both sinks short by different amounts' shape LEVEL_4's CONTROL A hits at its slider floor, without importing levels/level4.mjs. Could not execute `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs` in-turn (no Bash grant); every existing and new assertion was hand-traced against feasible()'s already-proven achieved/deficits algebra (3 = 10*0.3, 7 = 10*0.7, margins -0.4/-0.125) and against the unmodified string-formatting logic for the single-deficit and zero-deficit cases.

beads.title: verdictLine()'s ok-path margin is always the GLOBAL min-margin sink, unnamed — a player can't tell which sink is the tight one on a multi-sink level

beads.title: The loop critiqued its own optimal solution for removing the player's decision — no gate could have caught that, the vision did
beads.body:
The best thing this loop has produced, and it is a critique of its own previous turn.

Turn 15 built autoSplit() — the fan-out unlock, a closed-form provably-optimal split for a qualifying subcase, with the exchange argument stated. Turn 16 wired it into level 4. Correct work, and the mutation testing held (equal-split instead of demand-proportional kills both suites).

Then a later turn read the vision again and wrote level5.mjs, whose header says:

  "LEVEL_4 fans one source out to two sinks, but the split itself comes from
   autoSplit() — proportional to demand, no lever a player can move. Vision
   priority 1 calls the actual decision 'splitting a shared output between
   competing consumers... the genre's central decision', and autoSplit removes
   exactly that decision from the player's hands."

It noticed that its own mathematically-correct solution had automated away the thing the vision said mattered. The optimal split is the right answer to "is this satisfiable"; it is the WRONG answer to "what should the player decide", because a puzzle whose optimum is computed for you is not a puzzle. So level 5 uses the explicit per-edge share instead, and the player chooses.

Measured, the level is real:

  share 0.20/0.80 -> LOSE  fieldA short by 10
  share 0.45/0.55 -> OK    margin 0.100
  share 0.50/0.50 -> OK    margin 0.000
  share 0.80/0.20 -> LOSE  fieldB short by 30

A narrow winnable band with a DIFFERENT failure on each side. Err toward A and B starves; err toward B and A starves. That is a decision with consequences in both directions, which is what makes it a choice rather than a slider with one wrong end.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE LEVEL. Every safeguard in this system is aimed at catching work that is WRONG. Nothing in it can catch work that is correct and beside the point — the gate passes, the judge scores it, the deploy publishes it. autoSplit passed everything and still moved away from the goal.

What caught it was not a gate. It was an agent re-reading the operator's stated intent and noticing a conflict between that intent and an artefact the system had already accepted. That is the vision file doing the one job no gate can do, and it is the strongest evidence so far that the steering channel is load-bearing rather than decorative.

beads.title: Every seat's push loop died on a conflict in a GENERATED file — three stalls in five hours, and the retry was a spin not a retry
beads.body:
The five-hour run stalled three times and all three were the same thing. The last one is the clearest: at 10:05 the planner ran, thought for six minutes, proposed work, applied it to the ledger — and then "Commit the proposals" failed for 31 seconds and exited. Thirty-one seconds is exactly 2+4+8+16, the backoff loop exhausting itself.

THE PUSH LOOP CANNOT SURVIVE A CONFLICT IN A GENERATED FILE.

    git pull --rebase origin "$BRANCH" && git push origin HEAD:"$BRANCH"

loop/data/graph.json is DERIVED from the ledger. Two writers regenerate it from different states, so it conflicts on essentially every concurrent push. The rebase halts with the file unmerged, the `&&` short-circuits, and the next attempt runs `git pull --rebase` again — which now fails immediately because a rebase is already in progress. Four identical failures with sleeps between them. The retry looked like resilience and was a spin, which is the SAME defect as lp-95423f (a bare push retried four times), rediscovered in the layer above.

Fixed in all five committing workflows with the rule this repo already wrote down for exactly this — LOOP-SPRINTS.md's REDO, DO NOT RESOLVE. On a conflict: regenerate the derived file, stage, continue the rebase. Merging a generated file is never right; the generator is the resolution.

WHAT THIS COST, and it is the honest number: three stalls in five hours, and the whole content of at least one full planning turn (six minutes of model time, one proposal set, lost). It also explains why the run appeared to stop dead each time I pushed something — my own commits were the concurrent writer. The operator working alongside the loop was, structurally, the loop's main source of failure.

THE PATTERN IS NOW FIVE INSTANCES DEEP (lp-a4030e, lp-3d6bd4):

  1. the brief taught creates-gate; the outbox had no field for it
  2. the reviewer could not wake the tick on a zero-promote
  3. the worker's propose schema omitted class/gate
  4. the planner could not wake the tick at all
  5. every seat's push loop could not survive a conflict in a generated file

Five different components, one shape: the thing worked and the CHANNEL between it and the next stage could not carry the result. Every symptom was silence — a completed turn whose output went nowhere — because none of these failures throws where anyone is looking.

The generalisable rule, stated as sharply as I can: IN A SYSTEM WHOSE COMPONENTS COMMUNICATE THROUGH ARTEFACTS, THE ARTEFACTS ARE THE SYSTEM. Every one of these bugs was in a seam, not in a component, and every component's own tests passed throughout. A test suite that covers each part and no joint will report perfect health while nothing works end to end.

Repeating the standing recommendation: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn. Given the count is now approaching twenty, this is squarely a loop-work.yml workflow-level fix, not a per-turn note -- every future turn that repeats this note instead of fixing the workflow is spending a turn's worth of ledger space restating a known problem.

beads.title: Seeded the `next` Map from level.nodes, not from level.edges, so every node gets an array even with zero outgoing edges
beads.body: The old code built `next` purely from level.edges (`new Map(level.edges.map(e => [e.from, e.to]))`), so a node with zero outgoing edges (every sink) simply had no key in the Map at all -- fine for a single-value Map since a missing key and an empty result behave the same at the call site. For the array version I instead seed one entry per node from level.nodes first, then push edges into the corresponding array, so `next.get(id)` never returns undefined for a real node. This costs one extra pass over level.nodes but means the arrow loop's `for (const [fromId, toIds] of next)` also now iterates in level.nodes order rather than edges' first-occurrence order, and iterates every node including sinks that draw zero arrows (an empty inner loop, no cost). Rejected keeping edges-only construction with a `next.get(fromId) || []` fallback at the call site: it works identically but the seeded-from-nodes version means the Map's own shape now matches every other Map in this function (incoming, pos), which are all seeded from level.nodes first -- consistency with the file's existing convention, not a correctness requirement. Reversible in one line if a future turn prefers the edges-only construction; nothing else depends on `next`'s iteration order or its handling of zero-outgoing-edge nodes.

asks.title: Does explicit-share fan-out (levels 4 & 5, shipped) satisfy vision item 1's 'the real puzzle', or is the general multi-hop LP still the priority?
asks.body:
vision.md's item 1 was written against production.mjs v1, which refused fan-out outright — the file explicitly says 'every level so far is a straight line... by force, not by choice.' Since then (per the ledger: turns 15-16, lp-34239d and follow-ons) production.mjs grew explicit-share fan-out and autoSplit()'s closed-form proportional split, and levels 4 and 5 shipped exercising both — one automatic, one player-set. But production.mjs's own header is explicit that this is 'a deliberate, narrower feature than a general LP': a fan-out into PROCESSORS, or a sink fed by MORE than one supplier, still 'needs a real linear program over the whole network and is deliberately left alone.' That's a multi-turn build, not a one-turn ticket, and nobody has picked it up — possibly because it's genuinely too large for the current per-turn shape, possibly because levels 4/5 already answered the vision's concern and nobody said so.

DO: Open plant.minomobi.com and play levels 4 and 5 for a couple of minutes — level 4's automatic proportional split, level 5's player-set share slider between fieldA and fieldB.

WATCH FOR: Whether deciding where a shared output goes feels like 'the genre's central decision' vision item 1 names, or whether it still feels like tuning a slider toward a formula the game already knows the answer to.

SO THAT: If it reads as satisfying item 1: future turns should stop budgeting toward the general multi-hop LP and move fully to placement/gate 6 work instead, and vision.md's item 1 should be marked closed the same way gate 5 and levels 1-3 already are. If it does NOT: the next several turns need to start actually budgeting toward the general LP as a multi-turn arc (starting with, e.g., just the 'fan-out into processors with a single downstream sink each' sub-case) rather than continuing to look for more closed-form autoSplit() special cases one ticket at a time.

asks.title: Why were LEVEL_4, LEVEL_5, and LEVEL_6 each rejected-by-review with no reason recorded?
asks.body:
Three level proposals — LEVEL_4 (lp-9626f7, convergence: two sources into one processor), LEVEL_5 (lp-6aeecf, two independent sinks), LEVEL_6 (lp-b5e73b, an illegal-wiring refusal state) — were each written carefully against a real gap in what a shipped level exercises, each cited the same house style and CONTROL discipline as the levels that DID land, and each came back tagged rejected-by-review with nothing else recorded in the ledger. This turn deliberately avoided proposing a fourth level (a genuine fan-out-split level, which vision's own priority 1 is pointing straight at, and which is now newly buildable since turn 15 landed explicit-share fan-out) because I cannot tell from here whether the pattern is 'levels are the wrong shape of work right now' or something narrower each of the three happened to share.

DO: Open the three rejected beads (lp-9626f7, lp-6aeecf, lp-b5e73b) and say one sentence each on why, or point at wherever the review reason actually lives if it isn't in the ledger body.

WATCH FOR: Whether the reason is about LEVELS as a category right now (too much explainer-polish, or simply not wanted until fan-out/placement lands) versus something narrower each proposal happened to share (e.g. all three touched index.html in the same way, or all three were written against an older vision.md revision that has since changed).

SO THAT: If it's category-level, I stop proposing new levels entirely until told otherwise and put remaining planning budget into the oracle (autoSplit, placement-in-a-pocket). If it's narrower, I write the fan-out-split level next turn deliberately avoiding whatever the three shared, instead of guessing a fourth time.

asks.title: Level 3 never shows which of the two capacities is currently binding — is that ambiguity good friction or bad confusion?
asks.body:
Level 1 and Level 2 each have exactly one thing that can be wrong, so the verdict line alone always explains the failure. Level 3 has two independent capacities and the page deliberately does not highlight which one is currently the tighter constraint (per the ticket's own explicit decision to not expose production.mjs's per-node achieved rates this turn) — a visitor sees 'depot short by N' and has to experiment with both sliders to find out why. That could read as the level's whole point (forcing you to form a hypothesis and test it, which is closer to the vision's playability bar than a single slider ever was) or as it just being confusing on a small phone screen with two sliders and one vague error.

DO: Open plant.minomobi.com, scroll to Level 3, and drag only ONE slider at a time without reading this ask first — see how many drags it takes before you understand which knob you moved actually caused the change.

WATCH FOR: Whether you instinctively drag both sliders at once to 'search' for the answer, versus isolating one variable at a time the way the CONTROL structure in the test does.

SO THAT: If it reads as fine friction, Level 4 (convergence, proposed above) can ship with the same no-highlight approach. If it reads as confusing, the next level turn should add a lightweight per-processor 'binding' indicator (e.g. bold the capacity number that currently equals the achieved output) before building a fourth level with the same blind-spot.

asks.title: Does picking a labelled machine (its capacity printed right on the button) read as a production decision, or as arithmetic-checking?
asks.body:
LEVEL_2 (proposed this turn) replaces LEVEL_1's continuous ore-rate slider with three buttons, each showing the candidate machine's exact capacity number. That gets away from 'a slider that turns a label red', which is what ask lp-02e2be already questioned about LEVEL_1 — but it may trade one non-answer for another: if the capacity number is printed on the button, the 'puzzle' might just be 'which number is >= 50', solved by mental arithmetic before the click ever happens, rather than felt as installing different equipment. A machine cannot tell the difference between a real decision and a math check with extra steps.

DO: Once LEVEL_2 ships, open plant.minomobi.com, scroll to 'Level 2 — pick the machine', and click each of the three smelter buttons in turn.

WATCH FOR: Whether you catch yourself doing the subtraction (capacity minus 50) in your head before clicking, versus just trying options and reading the verdict.

SO THAT: If it still reads as arithmetic-checking, the next turn hides the capacity number and shows only the qualitative label (cheap/good/golden), so the number has to be discovered by trying it rather than read off the button — a bigger, different UI change I am not making speculatively this turn. If it reads as a real choice, LEVEL_2 ships as designed and the same three-option pattern is reused for future levels.

asks.title: Why were the two placement-legality modules and the band-colour ticket rejected?
asks.body:
Three consecutive proposals adjacent to priorities 2/3 were tagged rejected-by-review in beads.jsonl with no reason recorded: lp-7b7f04 (combined session-local placement legality + feasibility composition), lp-439104 (placement legality alone, deliberately split from lp-7b7f04 to isolate the problem), and lp-64a447 (a CSS class coloring the already-shipped band() label). All three read as Definition-of-Ready-complete from their bead text alone — named class, gate, bounded paths. Without the reason, I cannot tell whether this means 'stop proposing synthetic session-local placement entirely until the real foamworld pocket port lands' (lp-39d6e7 is then the only path back into priority 2), or 'something specific was wrong with those two tickets' (wording, a missed edge case, an implementation risk not visible from the ticket text alone) — and guessing wrong either wastes a future turn repeating the same rejected pattern, or wrongly avoids a category of work that was actually fine.

DO: Open the three rejected bead bodies (lp-7b7f04, lp-439104, lp-64a447) and whatever diff a worker produced against them, if one exists, and say which of the two readings is closer.

WATCH FOR: Whether the rejection reads as 'wrong category of work' (more scaffolding/inspector, not the game) versus 'right idea, wrong execution' (something specific in the ticket text or the resulting diff).

SO THAT: If it's category: future planning turns stop proposing any placement/legality module until lp-39d6e7's real-pocket port is scoped and landed, and I will say so explicitly rather than re-splitting the same idea a third way. If it's execution: I need the specific complaint so the next attempt at that category doesn't repeat it.

asks.title: Does LEVEL_1's ore slider satisfy 'not a slider that turns a label red', or is it exactly what that bar rules out?
asks.body:
The vision's bar for playable says: 'Not a slider that turns a label red — an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for.' LEVEL_1 (plant/levels/level1.mjs, wired into plant/index.html via level-view.js) is, literally, a continuous ore-rate slider that turns the verdict red when dragged far enough. It may already be exactly the thing that sentence warns against, or it may be an acceptable interim step given priority 2 (real-pocket placement) is currently blocked by foamworld.js's size (700+ lines, far past one turn to port — see this bead's decisions). I cannot tell which reading is intended, and it also bears on why lp-7b7f04 (a session-local placement+feasibility module, one level up from LEVEL_1's single slider) was rejected without a recorded reason — the two questions may have the same answer.

DO: Open plant/index.html (or plant.minomobi.com once deployed), scroll to 'Level 1', and drag the ore slider down until the verdict turns red.

WATCH FOR: Whether that moment reads as forming an intention and getting refused, or as watching a number cross a threshold — the two things the vision explicitly distinguishes.

SO THAT: If it reads as just a threshold, the next turn should stop extending slider-driven level logic (including this turn's placement.mjs) and instead scope a genuinely discrete click-to-place interaction, even a fabricated stand-in world. If it reads as acceptable for now, further turns can keep extending LEVEL_1-style levels — more nodes, more sinks, the band() dial this turn surfaces — without second-guessing the interaction model.

asks.title: Does the new self-compatibility fail state read as a build constraint, or as a broken slider?
asks.body:
Proposal 1 above adds a real fail state to the summon inspector — drag the inradius slider down and a solid flips from buildable to not, using the same rule reformPocket enforces elsewhere. But it is surfaced on a raw parameter slider in what is still a library page, not inside anything resembling a level, and I cannot tell from here whether that reads as 'the world has a build constraint you're bumping into' or as 'I turned a dial and got an error message'. This is one layer up from the already-open lp-7c8e6f (whether the anisotropic squash itself should be felt or hidden) — this one is about whether the FAIL STATE built on top of it lands as a mechanic.

DO: Once proposal 1 ships to plant.minomobi.com, pick icosahedron and drag the inradius slider down until the new buildable line flips from green to red.

WATCH FOR: Whether you instinctively try to fix it (raise r back up) before reading why it failed, or read the reason first — that's the difference between it landing as a mechanic and landing as noise.

SO THAT: If it reads as a mechanic, I'll keep proposing small inspector-scoped playability tickets like this one while lp-f25c2f/lp-39d6e7 are still in flight. If it reads as noise, I'll stop proposing anything UI-facing in plant/ next turn and only propose class-d analysis work until a real pocket exists to build an actual level against.

asks.title: Is the anisotropic squash something a player should FEEL, or something the game should hide?
asks.body:
Every summon so far is exact under a metric with aniso 2.2, so a solid is visibly squashed along Y. I cannot decide from here whether that reads as a deliberate material property of the foam — a thing you learn to exploit — or as a rendering bug the player fights. No gate measures this and either reading is internally consistent, so guessing sets the direction for every mechanic built on top of it.

DO: Open foam, summon a dodecahedron and an icosahedron side by side, and walk around them for a minute at eye level.

WATCH FOR: Whether the squash reads as the world having a grain you could use, or as the shapes being wrong.

SO THAT: If it reads as grain, I propose mechanics that USE the anisotropy — a source that only aligns along Y, a defense that is cheaper across the grain. If it reads as wrong, I propose a compensation pass that renders solids round while keeping the seed geometry exact, and the anisotropy stays a hidden implementation detail.
